mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns remain positive in >40% of cases when UNRATE exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) is high and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low, it indicates a potential policy mismatch, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of cases when CPIAUCSL is high and FEDFUNDS is low.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) signals weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns remain positive in >40% of cases when GDPC1 growth slows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of rising INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is high, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in >30% of cases when UNRATE is low and PAYEMS is high.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when RSAFS growth exceeds 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) increase borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns remain positive in >40% of cases during monetary tightening.
